'''''Euphorbia peplis''''', the '''purple spurge''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> is a species of ''[[Euphorbia]]'', native to southern and western [[Europe]], northern [[Africa]], and southwestern [[Asia]], where it typically grows on [[coast]]al sand and shingle.<ref name=grin>{{GRIN | access-date = 21 January 2018}}</ref><ref name="FEU"/><ref name="blamey">Blamey, M. & Grey-Wilson, C. (1989). ''Flora of Britain and Northern Europe''. {{ISBN|0-340-40170-2}}</ref>

==Description==
A small, prostrate, hairless [[annual plant]], the stems growing to {{convert|10–20|cm|in|0|abbr=on}} long, typically with four stems from the base. The [[leaf|leaves]] are opposite, oval, {{convert|1–2|cm|in|1|abbr=on}} long, grey-green, somewhat fleshy, reddish-purple veined, with oblique bases and a somewhat curved and wavy shape. Fruit capsules hairless, containing smooth 3mm seeds.<ref name="FoT">{{cite book |title=Flora of Turkey and the East Aegean Islands, vol. 7 |author=Davis}}</ref><ref name="FEU">{{cite book |title=Flora Europaea, vol. 2 |author=Tutin}}</ref>

==Habitat==
Sandy sea-shores, rarely inland.<ref name="FEU"/>

==Range==
Shores of the Mediterranean, Black, Caspian and Red Seas, Persian Gulf, Ireland ([https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:347719-1 PoWo Map])

At the northern edge of its range in [[England]], it has always been rare, and is now [[extinct]].<ref name="blamey"/><ref name="pearman">Pearman, D. A. & Preston, C. D. (2002). The last British record of Euphorbia peplis. ''BSBI News'' 91: 25.</ref>
